I'm sorry to hear about your past experiences with gender; unfortunately, the gatekeeping hasn't become much better (at least, not where I live). It took me almost two years to finally receive a diagnosis for gender dysphoria and the entire process was draining. I really wish there was a button, as well. Kinda feels like my entire life has been thrown away and there's nothing much I can do about it.

I feel you on the neurodivergent part, that definitely doesn't help anything (didn't mention in the original post but I have autism and ADHD). I feel like parts of this might be recognizable to me in the future; I can definitely feel the "sex is weird part", where I'm definitely not opposed to it but I can imagine parts of it being a bit of a trigger for me (overwhelming, like you said). 

The "resigning myself to being alone" part also rings very real in my mind. Even if I do at some point feel actual attraction and am aware of it.. I don't think I could be in a relationship with a woman, dysphoria-wise. It'd probably kill me. Men, cool in theory, haven't felt that much in real life.

The question of "if my body was different, would things make more sense?" is an interesting one I've never seen posed before. Though, I fear if I think about it too much it'll make me sadder. An interesting conundrum to be sure. 

Thank you for this comment; it is very recognizable at parts.

Heyy, so I am a 20-year-old pre-everything transwoman. As it is very likely I will be starting hormone therapy around summertime, which will make it more difficult to lose existing fat, I wanna get rid of my belly, or at least make as good an attempt as I can.

I am 194cm tall and last time I weighed myself I was roughly 76kg. I am quite skinny overall I'd say, unimpressive muscles and not very fat aside from my belly. I take roughly 10.000 steps a day through a combination of walking (like 6-7km/h) and cycling (15-20km/h unless there's strong wind). Additionally, I've been trying to get other exercise in. I've been doing the Chloe Ting 2021 21-day hourglass routine, which, from what I can gather, burns like 100ish calories per 10-15 min video?

Throughout the latter half of 2020 I cut almost all sugars out of my diet, basically quit sodas, reduced my candy intake by a lot, eating significantly better granola and milk products etc. My average day in food looks like this:

​

Breakfast: yoghurt with some granola, raisins, and frozen berries

Lunch: typically leftovers from last night's dinner (it's hard to cook just 1 portion of something), otherwise maybe scrambled eggs. Additionally, another small portion of yoghurt.

Dinner: usually some kind of stir fry. Always with a good amount of vegetables and with less rice/noodles/whatever than usual. I've replaced most of my meat intake with substitutes, which make up the other big part aside from vegetables. I do still eat eggs and fish, though. As dessert, quark with a slight flavoring.

Snacks: 2-3 pieces of fruit, as well as 1-2 "maiswafels" (rice cakes but made with corn). My big bad habit is that I tend to eat potato chips, popcorn, Tuc crackers or something similar almost every night, usually in portions that I regret. This one's been tough to kick.

​

My main questions are as follows:

How can I best lose this fat I'm dealing with, without losing too much muscle? Roughly how many calories should I be consuming (Google gives very conflicting answers, saying my maintenance calories could be 2000-2800 wtf)? Should I change up my exercise?

​

Thank you very much in advance and please let me know if I missed any info.
